human_tolerance.notes: Described as a common, noisy and conspicuous bird that occupies urban areas as readily as open grassland with scattered trees, and hunts from an exposed perch.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Judgement. The article gives clutch size, incubation and nestling periods but no calendar window for the region; a spring-to-early-summer window is used for the southern-hemisphere breeding season.

vocalizations.description: The exuberant three-syllable 'BEE-tee-WEE' the species is named for, given from an open perch; the bird has an onomatopoeic name in several languages.
A harsh, repeated scolding note given when a pair is disturbed at the nest, which the domed nest conceals behind its side entrance.

taxonomy.note: Rank and accepted name from the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy; Pitangus is a monotypic genus in the Tyrannidae.

external.note: GBIF usage key from the GBIF Backbone match for the scientific name; iNaturalist taxon id and Wikidata Q-id from Wikidata.

conservation.note: The article's taxobox gives the IUCN status as LC.

range.note: 'Its range extends from the Lower Rio Grande Valley in southern Texas south through Central America to southern Argentina. It does not regularly occur in Chile.' The country list is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 form of that sentence, with Chile omitted as stated.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'It is omnivorous and hunts like a shrike or flycatcher, waiting on an open perch high in a tree to sally out and catch insects in flight or to pounce' on the ground; the ground gait is therefore a hop and the bird flies between perches. Swimming and climbing are not described.

traits.nest_type.note: 'Both sexes build a large domed nest that has a side entrance.' A domed nest with a side entrance is a closed chamber, which the schema calls a cavity.

traits.perching.note: 'waiting on an open perch high in a tree to sally out' - the bird spends much of its foraging time perched.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits 1.0 BirdFuncDat row for Pitangus sulphuratus: BodyMass-Value 62.85 g.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: 'It is 25 to 28 cm in length and weighs 53 to 71.5 g.'

traits.wingspan_m.note: Neither Wikipedia article states a wingspan. Derived as roughly 1.13x body length (0.265 m), the usual span-to-length ratio for a medium tyrant flycatcher with long wings, giving about 0.30 m. This is an approximation, not a sourced figure.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No open-licensed source gives a typical or maximum lifespan for Pitangus sulphuratus: the English and Spanish Wikipedia articles, Wikidata and GBIF carry none, and the field-guide and Animal Diversity Web pages were avoided under the licence policy. 6.0 years is a documented judgement placeholder, not a sourced figure.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits 1.0 Diet-Inv 40, Diet-Vend 10, Diet-Vect 10, Diet-Vfish 10, Diet-Fruit 30 (BirdFuncDat row, Diet-Certainty A); Diet-Vend, Diet-Vect and Diet-Vfish are combined into the schema's vertebrate share. The article's 'it is omnivorous' and its account of catching lizards, insects and small vertebrates are consistent.

traits.social.note: 'Great kiskadees are monogamous and defend a territory.' group_size is fixed at the pair.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits 1.0 Nocturnal 0; the article describes daytime perching and sallying.

traits.defense.note: Authored: the bird flushes from its perch to a tree when approached, the escape the shared perching-songbird program encodes.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from its described occurrence in urban areas and its habit of hunting from an open, conspicuous perch.

habitat.use.note: ForStrat-ground 50, ForStrat-understory 40, ForStrat-midhigh 10; ground and understory are mapped to ground and arboreal and the mid-high share is dropped, so the two kept shares are renormalised to 0.5/0.5.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts and pauses in trees and shrubs between sallies; the domed nest is the breeding shelter.

habitat.resources.note: Prey weights follow the EltonTraits diet shares; the perch and shrub tags follow the described hunting and nesting sites, and nest_cup stands for the domed nest built of grasses and twigs.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: urban_affinity and uses_gardens from 'the great kiskadee occupies a wide range of habitats, from open grassland with scattered trees to urban areas'; road_mortality and light_max are judgement.

seasonal.strategy.note: The species is resident across its range and the article describes year-round territorial and breeding behaviour with no migration or hibernation.

seasonal.phases.note: The article gives 'The clutch is 3 to 4 eggs', a 16-17 day incubation and a 17-18 day nestling period but no calendar window; the phase dates are a judgement for the southern-hemisphere spring and summer.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Incubation 16-17 days plus a 17-18 day nestling period gives about 35 days to fledging; duration_days 40 adds the pre-fledging period, and scale is a judgement for a recently fledged bird.

vocalizations.song.note: 'The call is an exuberant BEE-tee-WEE, and the bird has an onomatopoeic name in different languages.'

vocalizations.alarm.note: The article describes the species as noisy and gives the harsh scolding notes used against intruders at the nest; the description is written from that account.

look.note: 'The head is black with a strong white supercilium and a concealed yellow crown stripe. The upperparts are brown, and the wings and tail are brown with usually strong rufous fringes. The bill is short, thick, and black in color.' Proportions and extra-part placement are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: invertebrate-based sallying from a perch, an October-December nest-building window, and a moderate flee distance for a bird that works in the open.
